parameters.name: DnListFileUrl
parameters.description:
The URL of the device list file for targeted updates.
> - When you initiate a targeted update (`TargetSelection=SPECIFIC`) task, you must specify this parameter or **TargetDeviceName.N**. You cannot specify both.
> - Call [GenerateDeviceNameListURL](~~186062~~) to generate the file URL and upload the device list file as instructed.
> - For a full update, devices that have already been updated are filtered out from the list.
> - For a delta update, devices that have already been updated and devices whose current version does not match the source version of the update package are filtered out from the list.

parameters.name: DownloadProtocol
parameters.description:
The protocol used to download over-the-air update package. Valid values: **HTTPS** (default) and **MQTT**. After the device receives over-the-air update package download information pushed by IoT Platform, the device uses this protocol to download over-the-air update package.

><notice>To use the MQTT protocol to download update packages, the following conditions must be met:
- Supported regions: China (Shanghai), China (Beijing), and China (Shenzhen) only.
- OTA update package: contains only one file, and the file size does not exceed 16 MB.
- Device SDK: You must use the latest version of the C language Link SDK provided by IoT Platform to develop OTA update and MQTT file download capabilities. For more information, see [OTA update code sample for downloading update packages by using the MQTT protocol](~~330985~~).

></notice>

parameters.name: FirmwareId
parameters.description:
The ID of the update package. The ID uniquely identifies the update package.

The update package ID is one of the parameters returned when you call [CreateOTAFirmware](~~147311~~) to create the update package.

You can call [ListOTAFirmware](~~147450~~) to view the update package ID from the response parameters.

parameters.name: GrayPercent
parameters.description:
The canary update percentage. The value is a percentage in string format with up to 3 decimal places. The system rounds down the calculated result. At least 1 device must be included in the canary update.

For example, if there are 100 devices pending update and the canary percentage is set to 33.33, the system calculates the result as 33.

This parameter is required when the update scope is set to canary update (`TargetSelection=GRAY`).

parameters.name: GroupId
parameters.description:
The group ID.

This parameter and **GroupType** are required only when you initiate a group update (`TargetSelection=GROUP`) task.


You can call [QueryDeviceGroupList](~~93356~~) to query the group ID (**GroupId**).

parameters.name: GroupType
parameters.description:
The group type. The only valid value is **LINK_PLATFORM**.

This parameter and **GroupId** are required only when you initiate a group update (`TargetSelection=GROUP`) task.

parameters.name: IotInstanceId
parameters.description:
The instance ID. On the **Overview** page in the IoT Platform console, view the **ID** of the current instance.

><notice>
- If this ID value exists, you must specify it. Otherwise, the call fails.
- If no <props="intl"><ph>**Overview** page or </ph></props>ID value is available, you do not need to specify this parameter.

></notice>

For more information about instances, see [Overview](~~356505~~).

parameters.name: MaximumPerMinute
parameters.description:
The maximum number of devices to which the download URL of the update package is pushed per minute. Valid values: 10 to 10000.

If you do not specify this parameter, the default value 10000 is used.

parameters.name: MultiModuleMode
parameters.description:
Specifies whether the device supports simultaneous multi-module upgrade.

- **false** (default): The device does not support simultaneous multi-module upgrade.
- **true**: The device supports simultaneous multi-module upgrade. In this case, **OverwriteMode** cannot be set to **2**. Upgrade nodes for the same module are overwritten, but nodes that are in progress are not overwritten.

><notice>
- Supported instances: Enterprise instances and new public instances.
- Device SDK: You must use the C language 4.x version of the Link SDK provided by IoT Platform.

></notice>

For more information, see [Description of simultaneous multi-module updates for devices](~~58328~~).

parameters.name: NeedConfirm
parameters.description:
Specifies whether to use a mobile app to control whether a device can perform an over-the-air update. You must develop the mobile app on your own.


- **false** (default): The over-the-air update node information is obtained based on the **NeedPush** parameter settings.
- **true**: The device cannot obtain the over-the-air update node. After the app confirms the over-the-air upgrade, the device can obtain the over-the-air update node information based on the **NeedPush** parameter settings.

parameters.name: NeedPush
parameters.description:
Specifies whether IoT Platform proactively pushes over-the-air update task to devices.

- **true** (default): IoT Platform proactively pushes over-the-air update task to online devices within over-the-air update scope after the batch task is created.
    
    In this case, devices can still proactively send requests to IoT Platform to obtain OTA update task information.

- **false**: Devices must send requests to IoT Platform to obtain OTA update task information.

parameters.name: OverwriteMode
parameters.description:
Specifies whether to overwrite the previous update task. Valid values:
- **1** (default): does not overwrite. If a device already has an update task, only the existing task is executed.
- **2**: overwrites. The device executes only the new update task. In this case, **MultiModuleMode** cannot be set to **true**.


> Update tasks that are in progress are not overwritten.

parameters.name: ProductKey
parameters.description: The **ProductKey** of the product to which the update package belongs.

parameters.name: RetryCount
parameters.description:
The number of automatic retries.

If you specify the **RetryInterval** parameter, you must specify this parameter.

Valid values:

- **1**: 1 time.
- **2**: 2 times.
- **5**: 5 times.

parameters.name: RetryInterval
parameters.description:
The automatic retry interval after a device fails to be updated. Unit: minutes. Valid values:

- **0**: retries immediately.
- **10**: retries after 10 minutes.
- **30**: retries after 30 minutes.
- **60**: retries after 60 minutes (1 hour).
- **1440**: retries after 1,440 minutes (24 hours).

><notice> The value of **RetryInterval** must be less than the value of **TimeoutInMinutes**. For example:
- If **TimeoutInMinutes** is set to 60 minutes, the maximum value of **RetryInterval** is 30.
- If **TimeoutInMinutes** is set to 1440 minutes, the maximum value of **RetryInterval** is 60.

If you want to set **RetryInterval** to retry after 24 hours, do not specify **TimeoutInMinutes**. After the update times out, no retry is triggered.
></notice>

If you do not specify this parameter, no retry is performed.

parameters.name: ScheduleFinishTime
parameters.description:
The time to end the update.

The end time must be at least 1 hour and at most 30 days after the start time (**ScheduleTime**). The value is a 13-digit timestamp in milliseconds.

If you do not specify this parameter, the update is not forcibly ended.

parameters.name: ScheduleTime
parameters.description:
The time to start the over-the-air update.

The scheduled time must be within the range of 5 minutes to 7 days from the current time. The value is a 13-digit UNIX timestamp in milliseconds.

If you do not specify this parameter, the upgrade starts immediately.

parameters.name: SrcVersion
parameters.description:
The list of source versions to be updated.

> - You can specify this parameter when you initiate a full update (`TargetSelection=ALL`) or canary update (`TargetSelection=GRAY`) task.
> - When you use a delta update package to initiate a full update or canary update task, set this parameter to the source version (**SrcVersion**) of the delta update package.
> - Do not specify this parameter when you initiate a targeted update (`TargetSelection=SPECIFIC`) or group update (`TargetSelection=GROUP`) task.
> - You can call [QueryDeviceDetail](~~69594~~) to view the OTA module version of a device (**FirmwareVersion**).
> - The list cannot contain duplicate version numbers.
> - You can specify up to 10 version numbers.

parameters.name: Tag
parameters.description: The list of tags.

sub_parameters.name: Key
sub_parameters.description:
The key of the batch tag. Only letters, digits, and periods (.) are supported. The key must be 1 to 30 characters in length. You can add up to 10 batch tags.

Batch tags are sent to devices when IoT Platform pushes update notifications.

> Batch tags are optional. The **Required** field is set to **Yes** because if you specify a batch tag, **Tag.N.Value** and **Tag.N.Key** must be specified in pairs.

sub_parameters.name: Value
sub_parameters.description:
The value of the batch tag. The value must be 1 to 1024 characters in length. You can add up to 10 batch tags. The total length of all batch tag keys and values cannot exceed 4,096 characters.


> Batch tags are optional. The **Required** field is set to **Yes** because if you specify a batch tag, **Tag.N.Value** and **Tag.N.Key** must be specified in pairs.

parameters.name: TargetDeviceName
parameters.description:
The list of device names for targeted updates.

> - When you initiate a targeted update (`TargetSelection=SPECIFIC`) task, you must specify this parameter or **DnListFileUrl**. You cannot specify both.
> - When you use a delta update package for a targeted update, the current OTA module version of the device must match the source version (**SrcVersion**) of the delta update package.
> - You can call [QueryDeviceDetail](~~69594~~) to view the OTA module version of a device (**FirmwareVersion**).
> - The devices in the list must belong to the same product as the update package.
> - The list cannot contain duplicate device names.
> - You can specify up to 200 device names.

parameters.name: TargetSelection
parameters.description:
The scope of the update.

- **ALL**: full update.
- **SPECIFIC**: targeted update.
- **GRAY**: canary update.
- **GROUP**: group update.

parameters.name: TimeoutInMinutes
parameters.description:
The timeout period for the device update. If the device does not complete the update within the specified time, the update fails. Unit: minutes. Valid values: 1 to 1440.

> - The time is calculated from when the device first reports the update progress. If the device goes online and offline multiple times during the update, which triggers IoT Platform to push the update package multiple times, the start time is always the time when the device first reports the update progress.
- An update failure caused by a timeout does not trigger the automatic retry logic.




If you do not specify this parameter, no timeout limit is imposed on the device update.
